reader_question: I added /config.local.json to the root .gitignore, but Git still shows changes to this already committed file. How do I stop tracking it while keeping my local copy?
reader_context: Git 2.50.0, normal checkout, commands run from the repository root. The file has no staged content changes. The project intends to stop versioning this file; this is not a request to hide local changes to a file everyone should keep tracking.

source_ledger.verbatim_excerpt: Working tree files, whether modified or not, will be left alone.

mandatory.claim: Ignore rules do not stop tracking a file already in the index.
Run git rm --cached -- config.local.json; it removes this index entry and keeps the working file.
Keep the ignore rule; stage .gitignore and commit the tracking removal with that rule.

mandatory_qualifications: The local copy stays on disk because --cached is present.
This changes repository tracking, not merely this user's display of changes.

optional_source_facts.claim: With --cached, indexed content must match HEAD or the working file; the stated context satisfies this check.
A leading slash makes the ignore pattern relative to this .gitignore file.
